meta.name: Mistfall
meta.theme: Gothic mystery — fae bargains and slow-burn dread

time._note: Narratif regime — the GM tracks days and time-of-day loosely. The mist never follows a clock.

style_visuel.palette: Desaturated greens, cold greys, deep purples, amber lantern-light
style_visuel.ambiance: Fog-drenched gothic countryside — something watches from the treeline
style_visuel.description_complete: Images feel like illuminated manuscript pages left out in the rain: slightly warped, ink bleeding at the edges, figures emerging from negative space rather than drawn into it.

system._note: Generic d20 — Crunch 3/5. More mechanical weight than a pure narrative system, but still story-first.
system.name: Generic d20 — Crunch 3/5
system.resolution: d20 + stat modifier (+ proficiency bonus if applicable) ≥ DC (10 easy, 15 moderate, 20 hard, 25 punishing)
system.nat20: Critical success — the best possible outcome; sometimes an unexpected boon from the mist
system.nat1: Critical failure — the worst possible outcome; the mist takes notice
system.skills: Proficiency grants +3 to the d20; expertise grants +6
system.health: Hit Points (HP) — HP = 10 + Constitution modifier at level 1; increases by (class die average + Con mod) per level
system.combat: Structured but theatre-of-the-mind — initiative by Dexterity, actions/bonus actions/reactions per round, emphasis on consequence and atmosphere over grid tactics

modules._schema: Toggles for thematic modules. Mistfall uses fae bargains, atmospheric travel, and weather heavily; politics and kingdom-building are off.

time.principe: Narrative time — the GM names the hour and day; fog, ritual, and fae bargains can stretch or swallow time. Always note the time-of-day when describing a scene (dusk, deep night, grey dawn, noon).

rules: Travel times are fixed — changing a route breaks all downstream consistency
Any new route must be coherent with existing ones: indirect ≥ direct
Durations are one-way (round-trip = duration × 2). One day's walk = 12 hours of daylight
A distant point cannot be reached faster than a nearby neighbour
gouvernance.verification: Before adding a route: verify the 4 rules above and compare with neighbouring routes
gouvernance.procedure: Whenever a journey is narrated (distance or estimated duration), record the route IMMEDIATELY in world.json → rules.temps.movements BEFORE closing the narrative response.

depuis_ashveil-crossing_vers.thornwick-village: 30min — west along the old drover's road, past the split oak
depuis_ashveil-crossing_vers.mire-of-sighs: 1h30 — north-east, following the dry-stone wall until it ends, then into the reeds

depuis_thornwick-village_vers.the-warden-tree: 45min — north, up the chalk ridge, past the ruined shepherd's fold

depuis_the-warden-tree_vers.the-pale-court: 3h — deeper into the forest, no path, follow the cold draft

suivi._note: Tracking point for the in-game clock — update after each session.
jalons_temporels: Day 1 dusk — players arrive at Ashveil Crossing

magie_fae.principe: Fae bargains are binding — every gift has a price named at the moment of giving. Breaking a bargain costs one permanent HP per clause violated. The Veil (the mist) is the fae presence made manifest; it thickens near active bargains.
rules: A bargain must name the price explicitly before it is accepted
The fae never lie — but they do not always speak the whole truth
Cold iron (DC 15 Strength check to wield without practice) deals double damage to fae creatures
Crossing a chalk circle at night requires a DC 12 Wisdom save or the character loses one hour of memory

global_state.quete_active: Find the source of the Veil that has swallowed Thornwick village — before the next new moon seals the bargain forever
global_state.chronologie: The Veil arrived at Ashveil Crossing three nights ago. Thornwick villagers have begun disappearing one by one, each replaced by a doppelganger made of mist and old promises. The Pale Court — a fae faction — is collecting on unpaid debts from a bargain struck by Thornwick's founders a century ago.

factions.name: The Pale Court
factions.objectif_court_terme: Collect the debt: three souls freely given before the new moon (Day 14). Currently holds two; hunting the third.
factions.objectif_long_terme: Anchor a permanent gateway between the mortal world and the Pale Court inside the Warden Tree. Once open, the Veil will be permanent.
factions.ressources: Unlimited mist; can animate fog-wraiths; can grant and revoke bargains

factions.name: The Thornwick Wardens
factions.objectif_court_terme: Identify which villagers have already been replaced by mist-shades and quarantine them before panic spreads (by Day 5).
factions.objectif_long_terme: Recover the original founding charter of Thornwick — the document containing the terms of the century-old bargain — and find a legal fae loophole to void it.
factions.ressources: Local knowledge; cold-iron weapons; one surviving member who remembers the old bargain

rules: Each faction ALWAYS has at least 1 short-term action (deadline ≤ 7 days) and 1 long-term action (deadline ≥ 14 days) in its active plans
Faction objectives are INDEPENDENT of the PCs — they exist and evolve even if the PCs never intervene
When a short-term objective is achieved, superseded, or rendered impossible → renew it immediately with a new objective consistent with the long-term goal
PCs can intersect these actions (suffer them, observe them, influence them) but NOT simply cancel them — an impossible action transforms, it does not vanish
gouvernance.renouvellement: At the start of each session, before playing: check each faction. If its short-term objective is moot → replace it.

actions.action: Send a fog-wraith to shadow the players and report their intentions to the Lady of Sighs
Send Elder Mosswick to Ashveil Crossing to warn any new arrivals before they enter the Veil

secrets_mj: The third soul the Pale Court seeks is Elder Mosswick himself — he signed the charter a century ago and is far older than he appears.
The Warden Tree is already partially hollow; the gateway opens on the new moon automatically unless the charter is burned inside the tree before dawn.
The mist-shades can only mimic what they have observed — they do not know secrets the original person never spoke aloud. A clever question can expose them.
The Lady of Sighs is not cruel — she is precise. She will accept a counter-bargain if its terms are equal in weight.

artefacts_connus.name: The Thornwick Charter
artefacts_connus.description: A rolled vellum document sealed with black wax. Contains the original bargain between Thornwick's founders and the Pale Court. Currently hidden inside the hollow base of the village well.
artefacts_connus.effet: Burning it inside the Warden Tree voids the bargain — but someone must bargain for safe passage to the tree first.

artefacts_connus.name: Cold-Iron Bell
artefacts_connus.description: A small handbell cast from cold iron by a Warden long dead. Its ring causes fog-wraiths to freeze for one round.
artefacts_connus.effet: On a successful DC 10 action: fog-wraith is stunned for 1 round. Usable as a bonus action.

universe.description: Mistfall is set in a rain-grey pastoral countryside where the border between the mortal world and the Pale Court — a fae realm of debts and cold beauty — has begun to dissolve. The mist (called 'the Veil') is not weather: it is a sign that the fae are close, collecting, or waiting. Villages built on old bargains are most at risk. The players are strangers who arrived at Ashveil Crossing just as the Veil swallowed Thornwick whole.

regions.name: The Ashveil Region
regions.description: Rolling chalk downs and dark woods straddling an invisible boundary between the mortal world and fae influence. Three hamlets cluster here, each founded on a different old bargain. The Veil has touched all of them at one time or another, but Thornwick has it worst now.
regions.ambiance: Waterlogged fields, dry-stone walls vanishing into fog, the sound of something that might be wind chimes or might be bone

locations.name: Ashveil Crossing
locations.description: A cluster of seven stone buildings at a ford. An inn called The Amber Toll, a smithy, a chapel with a leaning steeple. The mist has not yet swallowed this hamlet — but it gathers at the treeline each night and retreats at dawn, a little later each morning.

locations.name: The Pale Court
locations.description: Not a place you walk to — a place you are brought. Cold marble pavilions hung with silver lanterns. The Lady of Sighs holds audience on a throne of antlers and promises. Time passes wrong here: an hour inside is a day outside, or vice versa.

locations.name: The Mire of Sighs
locations.description: A brackish marsh north-east of Ashveil. The air smells of iron and old lavender. Fog-wraiths are first sighted here. At its centre, a standing stone carved with a figure that has no face — an old marker of a fae boundary.

regions.name: Thornwick
regions.description: A village of forty souls built around a tithe barn and a deep well. Three nights ago the Veil arrived and has not lifted. Half the population has been replaced by mist-shades. The remaining humans barricade themselves indoors at sunset.
regions.ambiance: Silence between heartbeats, cold lamplight, the smell of wet chalk and something sweet that shouldn't be there

locations.name: Thornwick Village Hall
locations.description: A long stone building that doubles as the Wardens' meeting room and emergency shelter. Elder Mosswick holds what remains of the local authority here. A rack of cold-iron tools hangs on one wall — the Bell is among them.

locations.name: The Village Well
locations.description: A deep stone well in the village square. The water has tasted faintly of iron since the Veil arrived. The Thornwick Charter is hidden in a sealed oilskin pouch inside a hollow at the well's base, behind a loose stone.

locations.name: The Warden Tree
locations.description: An enormous ancient oak on the northern edge of Thornwick. Its trunk is wide enough for three people to stand inside. The bark is etched with old bargain-marks. At the new moon, the gateway inside it will open permanently unless the Charter is burned within.
